relationship_to_initial_review.purpose: Resolve the one explicit citation lead left unreviewed under the original four-source cap.

source.citation: Stephen Kirkland, Yuqiao Li, John S. McAlister, and Xiaohong Zhang, Edge Addition and the Change in Kemeny's Constant, arXiv:2306.04005v2, revised 29 January 2025.

locators.finding: The paper analyzes the quantitative change in Kemeny's constant when one edge is added to an initial tree, including extremal increase and decrease.

locators.locator: PDF page 3, introduction immediately before Examples 1.1-1.3
locators.finding: The authors explicitly say that they exclusively consider finite simple undirected graphs and analyze adding an edge to a tree; 'adding an edge' is defined as connecting one pair of previously nonadjacent vertices.
For a tree T and graph G formed by adding one edge, Sections 3 and 4 bound the single difference K(G)-K(T).
The only located phrase 'two edges' concerns deleting two edges from a unicyclic graph to construct a two-tree spanning forest. It is unrelated to jointly adding two nonedges.

exact_relevance.assessment: This paper is methodologically adjacent single-edge work, not prior publication of the proposed two-edge synergy minimum or its finite census.

decision_effect.reason: The concrete citation lead contains no exact result that would make the proposed below-order-7 census a known reproduction.
decision_effect.novelty_boundary: The five-source bounded review still cannot establish global openness or publication novelty. A successful run must remain a candidate exact minimum-order computation pending a broader citation and expert review.

method_note: Only this one supplementary primary source was retrieved and inspected. No additional source expansion and no graph, matrix, or Kemeny computation occurred.
